newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch says no target set for NZ spending review.
newsitem.headline: Birch says no target set for NZ spending review.

text.p: The New Zealand government plans a timetabled review all its spending, but no target has yet been set for the level of desired savings, Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Tuesday evening.

"A further initiative that cuts right across the public sector is a thorough review of spending, announced in the Budget. A timetable for this is being put together now," Birch said in the text of a speech due to be delivered to an Auckland Rotary Club meeting.
"We are not attempting to set a target for across-the-board savings," Birch said.
He said ministers involved in the review wanted the support of their colleagues "to have a solid objective evaluation of the worth of the government's spending".
"We are looking for better value for money by improving the mix of programmes offered.
"Reprioritised spending will give us greater headroom for new initiatives and to further work on priorities set down in the coalition agreement," Birch said.
He said savings of just 0.3 percent on total government expenditure of NZ$35 billion would allow $100 million of new initiatives without increasing overall spending.

Other measures to reduce the cost, and improve the effectiveness of government spending, included a case-by-case review of Crown ownership of business assets, "privatisation on merit", and moves to improve competition in the electricity generation industry by considering a further split of state- owned power generator ECNZ, Birch said.
He said this government, like the last, aimed to leave more of the economy in private hands by 1999-2000.

Six strategic assets including ECNZ, national grid operator Transpower and NZ Post were protected from sale by the coalition agreement signed in December between the conservative National Party and nationalist New Zealand First.
